description:
FILED s479 (Fable, 2026-09-08) from the s473h merge-review probes.  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main a9f2a264 and on the s473h tree c8e8a848.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $cr = sub { 7 }; my $v = eval { ${$cr} }; print defined $v ? "[$v]" : "undef", " err=[$@]\n";
    perl:  undef err=[Not a SCALAR reference at ...]
    PCL:   [CODE(0x1)] err=[]          <- the scalar deref hands back the code ref itself, silently

WHY IT IS STILL THERE: s473h member 1 made `${$aryref}` / `${$hashref}` perl`s fatal through `%p-aggregate-referent-p` (asks `%p-ref-referent`, the REFERENT rule -- not a type sniff).  Its record says CODE stays EXCLUDED because the first attempt that included CODE failed all 15 rows of Pl/t/moo-01.t, "exactly as the code comment warned".  That is the thing to understand before widening: perl dies on `${$code}` unconditionally, so if Moo (or PCL`s Moo/Sub::Quote path) reaches a scalar deref of something PCL represents as a CODE box, either (a) PCL represents a SCALAR ref as a CODE box somewhere (a representation bug the exclusion hides), or (b) the emitter lowers some non-deref spelling (`$$code` in a string? `&$code`? a `${\ ...}`) into the same runtime entry.  Find which with the failing moo-01.t rows: reduce ONE row to a probe, look at what value reaches `%p-aggregate-referent-p` and from which emitted form.

FIX: after (a)/(b) is known, include CODE in the referent rule and fix the real cause; guard rows beside member 1`s in Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t (`${$cr}`, `@{$cr}`, `%{$cr}` all die; `&{$cr}` and `$cr->()` still call), inverse-verified.  `cl/` change -> the full sweep + companion op/ref.t.  SIZE: S-M (the moo-01.t dependency is the unknown).
=== DONE (s483a, 2026-09-13) ===

THE FINDING: neither (a) nor (b) as filed â a THIRD cause, the CHECK LEVEL.
s473h's own commit message (0146e790) names what its failing attempt was: "a
%p-wrong-referent-p \"SCALAR\" arm", i.e. a type sniff on the UNBOXED value.
Reconstructed here as `(functionp (unbox (unbox val)))` at p-cast-$: it fails
ALL 15 rows of Pl/t/moo-01.t, dying inside Sub::Quote's capture_unroll output
`my $trigger_for_w = ${$_[1]->{"$trigger_for_w"}};` â a capture whose scalar
HOLDS a code ref, which unboxed twice IS a bare function.  That is hypothesis
(a)'s shape, but visible only to a check that unboxes twice.  The REFERENT
rule stops one level higher (the capture's scalar BOX), so with CODE included
moo-01.t is 15/15.  Traced: all 133 p-cast-$ calls in the Moo run have a
BOXED referent (box(FN), box(HASH), box(nil), box(str)).
DO NOT RETRY: a type sniff on the unboxed (or double-unboxed) value at a
`${...}` site.  It is #154's ambiguity and it takes Moo down.

WHAT SHIPPED (two members):
1. %p-aggregate-referent-p -> %p-non-scalar-referent-p, CODE included; an
   UNBOXED operand is its own referent (`${\&named}`, `${sub{7}}`, a coderef
   read out of a HASH element arrive bare); the SAME guard added to
   (setf p-cast-$) â the write half was a silent wrong of its own
   (`${$aryref} = 5` wrote nowhere, `${$coderef} = 5` CLOBBERED the variable,
   so the next call through it died "Undefined subroutine &main::5").
2. Forced by the sweep, which is the bar the guards could not be: member 1 was
   gate-green and identical to perl over 40 probe shapes and still cost
   perl-tests/ref.t and postfixderef.t one row each.  ref.t:139
   (`$subrefref = \\&mysub2; is ($$subrefref->("GOOD"), "good")`) is a
   reference TO a code ref, and `\ CODEVALUE` was IDEMPOTENT â p-backslash's
   aggregate arm made box(FN), which is what a variable holding a code ref
   already is.  A raw function now takes the raw-VALUE arm (double box +
   is-ref), like \42; `\&NAME` never reaches p-backslash and
   p-backslash-sub-ref's direct branch (`\&$cr`) answers with the function
   itself.  Fixes a pre-existing silent wrong too: ref(\\&f) said CODE where
   perl says REF.

BARS: sweep GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL passing 18675 (+0),
drops 5 = census; ir-conform 321 pass / 0 fail / 24 known / 0 stale;
companion op/ ref-family leg = snapshot; gate green.  63 probe shapes vs perl
5.40.3 identical except #1618 and an address string.
GUARD: Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t 20 -> 30 rows (6 fail on the eabff00d
extraction, 4 negatives pass on both).  ir-spec: the ${...} fatal and the
p-backslash bullet are both normative.
FILED: #1618 ($coderef->[0] answers the code ref; p-aref-deref's functionp arm
serves the arrow subscript AND the list slice `(sub{..})[0]` â emitter work).
subject: `${$coderef}` (scalar deref of a CODE ref) returns the ref where perl dies "Not a SCALAR reference" -- the referent rule (#1249(1), s473h) EXCLUDES CODE because including it failed all 15 moo-01.t rows; the cause of that dependency is the finding
